normalization_policy: normalized claim plus artifact and evidence target; no voting

findings.claim: P14 makes the sealed bundle self-expire because P15 pins the current RootControlJournal lineage and remaining administrative-recovery allocation, while every required AdministrativeResourceLedger append first mutates and debits that journal; P14 permits mutable prefix growth only for the invalidation index and defines no corresponding RootControlJournal extension rule.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Bundle `bootstrap_authority` receipt re-hashes the HUMAN-accepted `AdministrativeLedgerGenesisReceipt`, complete genesis AIP/Workspace/RootControlJournal lineage and current finite administrative-recovery allocation
findings.impact: Prepare, sealing, intent, and accounting appends necessarily change a sealed P15 input, so a conforming implementation must either expire every bundle before charge or ignore required drift and charge against stale root-journal budget evidence.
findings.recommended_action: Define an explicit P14 RootControlJournal prefix-extension and reservation-scoped reconciliation rule: pin the sealed prefix, allow only contiguous entries for the same AdmissionResourceReservation, recompute debits and remaining recovery ceiling at the final writer boundary, and fail closed on unrelated, missing, or excess entries.

findings.claim: The AdministrativeResourceLedger append candidate is required to embed its own candidate/after-ledger hash while that hash identifies the same persisted candidate bytes, but the design defines no excluded-field or other non-self-referential hash domain.
findings.evidence_excerpt: The ledger candidate has one durable write, embeds all operation-receipt fields plus that root-entry hash/attempt ID, source/candidate hashes and the debited overhead, and its version-guarded atomic replacement makes the entry hash the receipt identity.
findings.impact: Candidate construction and deterministic validation are undefined or recursively self-referential, so the administrative ledger bootstrap cannot reliably produce the exact bytes required for P15 and different implementations could validate different receipts.
findings.recommended_action: Specify a non-self-referential canonical hash construction, such as hashing an explicitly defined entry body that excludes its `entry_hash`/after-ledger field and having the RootControlJournal bind the resulting full candidate hash before the write; distinguish that payload hash from the raw persisted-ledger hash in validation and recovery.

findings.claim: REVIEW_PENDING recovery may add a previously unbound route role/family without changing the packet, but route eligibility is fixed by the pre-charge substitution matrix and immutable review policy/template; no versioned policy-amendment artifact or ReviewClosureReceipt binding is defined for the newly eligible route.
findings.evidence_excerpt: A fresh HUMAN decision may add exact route roles/families and review-only call budget without changing packet/output/attempt
findings.impact: The coordinator can either dispatch outside the policy evidence later validated by ReviewClosureReceipt or remain unable to use the new route; the former can let an ineligible review contribute to acceptance closure and the latter leaves recovery non-operational.
findings.recommended_action: Keep the reviewer context packet byte-identical but define a separate append-only HUMAN route-authorization amendment record with prior-policy hash, exact role/family, eligibility and diversity proof, retry disposition, and no rubric/context change; require ReviewClosureReceipt to bind and validate the complete amendment chain and actual dispatch record.
